messages:
alice.sre: heads-up — since 03:00 UTC we've been seeing sustained shared-pool GPU saturation in eu-west-1. queue_depth for shared-pool-gpu > 800 for > 20m and p99 token latency jumped to ~5.2s. looks like one tenant is driving most of the backlog :/
ben.infra: which tenant? any model/id?
dave.prod: seeing tenant-olympus in the usage dashboard spiking to 68% of shared-pool capacity, running a mixture of 70B and 13B with long contexts. they also have lots of short-lived tiny requests, weirdly.
carol.runtime: short-lived tiny requests with large model sizes => very inefficient KV cache warming + lots of scheduling churn. that explains high queue depth even with moderate aggregate tokens.
eve-oncall: alerts started firing for cross-tenant SLA violations (users complaining). what's our stop-gap?
alice.sre: immediate: we should shape that tenant onto a burst/soft-throttle while we design a lasting policy. idea: credit-based shaping per-tenant that charges 'cost units' proportional to estimated GPU-time (model * seq_len) and enforces a leaky-bucket drain tied to current pool occupancy.
ben.infra: we already emit model_name and estimated_seq_len in request traces. could compute cost on the edge and set X-Cost-Units header for envoy ratelimit. quick hack: config change to limit tenant-olympus to 200 cost-units/s.
carol.runtime: +1. as long as we map cost-units to admission control tokens in the queueing layer. should also exempt small debug jobs.
dave.prod: what's the formula? OS/ops want something deterministic we can explain to customers.
carol.runtime: propose: cost_units = model_param_factor * max(seq_len, 32) * (req_type == streaming ? 0.6 : 1.0). model_param_factor: 70B=5, 13B=2, 7B=1.
ben.infra: OK. I'll draft an envoy rate-limit rule. snippet: ```yaml
- actions:
  - request_headers:
      header_name: "x-tenant-id"
  - generic_key:
      descriptor_value: "cost_units"
```
ben.infra: then in ratelimit service we accept cost-units and decrement the tenant bucket.
eve-oncall: what about noisy tenants that oscillate? we shouldn't thrash them between allowed and blocked. need slow-start/backoff after a throttle.
alice.sre: agreed. propose a circuit-breaker state machine per-tenant: OPEN -> HALF_OPEN after cool-down -> CLOSED. OPEN when their rolling drop rate > 30% and pool occupancy > 85%. HALF_OPEN allows a small share (burst credits) to probe.
dave.prod: can we auto-migrate persistent noisy tenants to a dedicated pool when they exceed a monthly cost threshold? that avoids repeated noisy-neighbor incidents and signals customers to buy Dedicated.
alice.sre: spelling: @dave.prod good call. add auto-migrate hook: if 3 sustained saturation windows in 24h and cost > X, mark for migration and notify account team.
carol.runtime: migration path needs pre-warm of KV cache. otherwise the dedicated tenant will temporarily spike the new pool. suggest we do a progressive split: move 20% traffic first (canary), warm cache, then cutover.
ben.infra: operationally we can create a best-effort pool (lower SLA) and a burst-dedicated pool (short-term reserved). we can fast-provision GPUs with our pool-autoscaler and label them dedicated:tenant-olympus. kubectl patch autoscaler ... will work as short-term.
alice.sre: also need to update billing so customers see surcharge for burst-dedicated. finance wants the metric in the invoice pipeline.
dave.prod: action items: 1) ben to add envoy ratelimit rule + cost_units mapping (ETA 2h). 2) carol to implement admission control mapping cost_units -> queue tokens (ETA 6h). 3) ben + infra to provide a quick script to spin dedicated burst pool (ETA 4h). 4) eve to watch for regressions (oncall).
eve-oncall: taking 4. I'll mute noncritical alerts for now and post updates in #incidents if we need paging.
ben.infra: quick deploy note — I'm pushing tenant-shaper v2 to staging now. deploy-bot: canary tenant-shaper v2 deployed to staging.
deploy-bot: canary deploy started by ben.infra at 1765004405 — status: success on staging.
alice.sre: once staging looks good, we can enable for eu-west-1 shared-pool only. conservative ramp: 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 30m windows.
carol.runtime: logging: add new metrics: tenant_cost_units_consumed, tenant_circuit_state, tenant_slowstart_credits_left. correlate with p99_token_latency.
dave.prod: also add customer-facing note: "We're introducing per-tenant shaping to improve fairness; heavier models may be charged higher cost units." keep wording friendly.
alice.sre: will draft the note. final: if anyone's blocked or wants to discuss algorithm tweaks, ping me. thanks all :thumbsup:
